chunks: Muhammad ibn Uthman narrated: Ibn Abi Khaythama narrated to me: Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn 'Ilqah, Sammak ibn Harb, and Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, all of them from Jabir ibn Samrah, that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'After me, there will be twelve caliphs.'
Then he spoke something that I did not understand. Some of them said: 'I asked the people, and they said: He said: All of them are from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve caliphs mentioned in the hadith and what is their lineage?
ai.summary: This foundational hadith, known as the 'Hadith al-Thalatha wa Ashara,' is cited by both Sunni and Shia scholars to establish the number of legitimate successors, with Shia tradition specifically identifying them as the Twelve Imams. The clarification that all are from Quraysh underscores the divine selection of leadership within the Prophet's tribe, a key criterion for Imamate in Shia jurisprudence. Al-Nu'mani’s inclusion of this narration in *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights its role in validating the eschatological timeline of the Imams' occultation and return.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (32) Muhammad bin Uthman narrated from ibn Abu Olaqa, Sammak bin Harb and Hussayn bin Khaythama from Ali bin al-Ja’d from Zuhayr bin Mo’awiya from Ziyad bin Abdurrahman from Jabir bin Samra that the Prophet (S) had said: “There will be twelve caliphs after me.”
Then he (the Prophet (S)) said something that I could not understand. Some people said that the Prophet (S) had said: “All of them are from Quraysh.”
